title: $17 an Hour Is How Much a Year? (2026)
metaDescription: $17/hour is $35,360 a year at 40 hrs/week — $2,947 monthly, $1,360.00 biweekly. See overtime pay tables and a 2026 federal take-home estimate.

hero.lede: Full time at 40 hours a week, 52 weeks a year (2,080 hours). Below: every pay-period equivalent, overtime tables at time-and-a-half, and a 2026 federal-only take-home estimate.

shortAnswer.heading: How much is $17 an hour per year?
shortAnswer.html: $17 an hour is $35,360 a year at 40 hours a week for 52 weeks (2,080 hours). That's $680.00 a week, $1,360.00 biweekly, and $2,946.67 a month gross. After estimated federal income tax and FICA, a single filer keeps about $30,592 — and steady overtime at $25.50/hour raises the total fast.

sections.title: What $17/hour adds up to per period.
sections.note: Gross (pre-tax) figures assuming paid hours every week of the year. Unpaid time off reduces them proportionally.

sections.title: $17 an hour in 2026, in plain numbers.
paragraphs: A $17/hour wage annualizes to $35,360 at full time ($17 × 2,080 hours). Hourly workers rarely see exactly that: unpaid days off pull it down, while overtime — paid at time-and-a-half — pushes it up fast.

That annual figure lands about 46% below the U.S. median full-time wage: BLS median weekly earnings are $1,251 (BLS, Q2 2026), which is roughly $31.28 an hour at 40 hours. Unlike most salaried roles, hourly jobs are usually overtime-eligible — see the table below for what that's worth.

sections.title: Overtime at $25.50/hour changes the math quickly.
sections.note: Overtime rows assume time-and-a-half (1.5 × $17 = $25.50) on hours past 40, every week of the year — the FLSA baseline for non-exempt workers.

sections.title: From $35,360 gross to take-home.
sections.note: Single filer, standard deduction, no state/local income tax, credits, or pre-tax benefits. Actual checks vary.

sections.title: What a single filer actually keeps.
paragraphs: After the 2026 standard deduction of $16,100, a single filer earning $35,360 owes about $2,063 in federal income tax (effective rate 5.8%, marginal bracket 12%) and $2,705 in Social Security and Medicare. That leaves roughly $30,592 — about $1,176.61 per biweekly check — before any state income tax.

faq.q: How much is $17 an hour per year?
faq.a: $17 an hour is $35,360 a year at full time — 40 hours a week for 52 weeks (2,080 hours). At 30 hours a week it comes to $26,520, and with 10 hours of weekly overtime it reaches about $48,620.

faq.q: How much is $17 an hour biweekly?
faq.a: A standard 80-hour biweekly period at $17/hour grosses $1,360.00. After estimated federal income tax and FICA for a single filer, roughly $1,176.61 remains per check, before state taxes.

faq.q: How much is $17 an hour after taxes?
faq.a: On $35,360 of annual wages, a single filer taking the 2026 standard deduction pays about $2,063 of federal income tax plus $2,705 of FICA, keeping roughly $30,592 a year — about $14.71 per hour worked. State and local taxes reduce this further where they apply.

faq.q: How much is $17 an hour with overtime?
faq.a: Overtime pays time-and-a-half: $25.50 per hour past 40 in a week. A steady 50-hour week earns $935.00 weekly — $48,620 a year, $13,260 more than the straight 40-hour year.

faq.q: Is $17 an hour a good wage in 2026?
faq.a: $17/hour annualizes to $35,360, which is about 46% below the U.S. median full-time wage — the BLS median for full-time workers is $1,251/week (about $31.28/hour, BLS, Q2 2026). Local cost of living, benefits, and schedule stability matter as much as the rate itself.

methodology: Annualization is straight arithmetic: $17 × 2,080 hours (40 hours × 52 weeks) = $35,360, with daily/weekly/biweekly/monthly rows derived the same way. No unpaid leave is assumed.
Overtime rows use the FLSA non-exempt baseline of 1.5× base pay ($25.50/hour) on hours over 40 per week, sustained all 52 weeks.
The take-home estimate uses 2026 federal brackets for a single filer with the $16,100 standard deduction plus employee FICA (7.65%). It excludes state/local tax, credits, and pre-tax benefits.
Median-wage comparison: BLS median usual weekly earnings, full-time workers, $1,251/week (BLS, Q2 2026).
